chapter_title: 第92章 五千塊的稿費

segments.title: 第92章 五千塊的稿費
segments.content:
Reigniting the Verdant Years Chapter 92: A Manuscript Fee of Five Thousand Yuan

At five-thirty in the evening, Li Guohong's family of three, along with Li Guoru's family of five, sat around the newly set-up round table and began to eat dinner.

In their Li family, Li Luo's grandfather was the eldest. He had two younger brothers and one younger sister, one of whom was the third grand-uncle who had sold them the house.

Below him, Li Luo's grandfather had a total of five children.

They were Li Guoru, the eldest; three aunts in the middle; and Li Guohong, the youngest.

Among them, the age gap between Li Guoru and Li Guohong was a full twenty years.

And in the year Li Guoru turned twenty, he happened to get married and have a child.

As a result, Li Guoru's son, Li Dao, was born in the same year as Li Guohong.

Because Li Guohong had better grades when he was young, he attended high school.

Li Dao, on the other hand, had been mischievous since childhood. He dropped out after one year of junior high, entered the workforce early, and got married a few years before Li Guohong.

Thus, Li Dao's son, Li Luo's nephew Li Xiang, was a generation younger than Li Luo, despite being three or four years older.

Although nowadays they didn't deliberately emphasize these things when they met, and Li Xiang usually didn't call Li Luo "uncle."

But it was still a bit awkward.

Li Luo used to find it awkward too, but after being reborn, his 35-year-old soul facing a little brat who had just started college suddenly felt that being called "uncle" wasn't so unacceptable.

But right now, Li Luo had no time to worry about such things.

After all, ever since he had returned home, the group had been discussing Li Luo's writing.

Once the three women also came to the table, the chatter became even more lively.

"Li Luo knows how to write?"

"What did he write?"

"It's already posted online?"

When asked these questions, Lin Xiuhong would help explain a little.

Li Luo felt like he was sitting on pins and needles as he ate, wishing he could find a hole to crawl into.

Fortunately, among the elders, most hadn't even finished junior high and had very limited education and knowledge, so Li Luo wasn't worried they would actually read his work.

But he couldn't guard against the one or two who just might.

Especially this eldest uncle of his.

Although he hadn't attended much school as a child, he learned to read with the help of a kind boss in his adult years.

Later, he traveled all over Qianjiang Province, doing various businesses, and his horizons gradually broadened. As he got older, he was still willing to continue learning and had read many books.

As his son Li Dao grew up, Li Guoru had originally wanted to slowly hand over the family business to him.

Who knew that Li Dao had little interest in inheriting the family business, and instead always wanted to venture out on his own.

After a long time, Li Guoru grew disheartened. He simply liquidated the company's assets, exchanged them for a few houses and storefronts, and then retired.

After retiring, Li Guoru had nothing to do. He was also getting on in years and thought to himself that he didn't want to be forgotten after he died, so he started writing his own memoirs and found someone to polish them.

Later, he spent a sum of money to self-publish through a publishing house and, with that, joined the Yuhang City Writers' Association.

Through these repeated activities, Li Guoru's life gradually settled down. Every day, he would go to the city writers' association's member center for a visit, drinking tea and chatting with people.

He just never expected that someone from the younger generation of his family would also have some interest in literature.

But after reading Li Luo's masterpiece, Li Guoru remained silent for a long time. Finally, at the lively dinner table, he said with careful consideration, "Li Luo."

Li Luo stopped eating and looked up at his eldest uncle, a look of confusion on his face.

Li Guoru paused for a moment, and after the table quieted down, he continued, "Your book, I've read a little of it."

"The quality, forgive me for being blunt, but if you put it in the writers' association, it would be unreadable."

"Of course, you're still young. Creation is something that needs to be done step by step, so there's no need to belittle yourself."

At this point, Li Guoru paused. Seeing that Li Luo was listening, he turned to Li Guohong and Lin Xiuhong next to him and said:

"Li Luo is still young and might not understand. And you two don't usually pay attention to this sort of thing, which is understandable, so I have to spell it out for you."

"This web novel thing, it's not on the same path as our traditional literature."

"Although it's all called writing, the content that comes out is worlds apart. And web content is something that can't be presented in public."

"If Li Luo wastes too much time on this, it'll really be a waste of energy."

"After all, he worked so hard to get into Fuyizhong. With a bit more effort, couldn't he get into Qianjiang University?"

"If he can get into Qianjiang University, what couldn't he do in the future?"

"When that time really comes, with a Qianjiang University diploma in hand and a good job found, if Li Luo is still interested in his spare time, it's fine for him to go write this web novel stuff then."

"You two don't know."

"In our Qianjiang Province's writers' association, web novel authors couldn't even join before."

"It's only this year that they've set up an exclusive online writers' association for web novels, but it's just a small organization affiliated with our provincial writers' association."

"Go ask other provinces, they don't have things like an online writers' association."

"If you take what you've written online to them, they won't even glance at it, and you can forget about joining."

At this point, Li Guoru took a deep breath. Seeing that everyone had fallen silent, he changed his tone, looked at Li Luo, and consoled him softly, "Eldest Uncle isn't targeting you, I'm just looking out for you."

"You've gotten into Fuyizhong now; all your future hopes lie here."

"Look at Li Xiang. He slacked off a bit just before the college entrance exams and missed his chance with Qianjiang University. What a pity that was."

"If you work hard these three years without any distractions, once you're admitted to Qianjiang University, your future will be a wide, open road, don't you think?"

To be honest, if anyone else had come to his house and said such things, Li Luo probably would have stood up and battled it out with them.

But since his eldest uncle was the one who said it, Li Luo kept quiet, merely nodding silently, hoping this topic would pass quickly.

In his past life, when Lin Xiuhong was seriously ill, his eldest uncle was also well advanced in years and plagued by illness, often having to go to the hospital.

When Lin Xiuhong was at her most critical, Li Guoru was also lying in a hospital room, yet he still didn't forget to instruct Li Dao to help contact some of the more famous doctors in Yuhang City.

Although his eldest uncle's words were unpleasant to hear right now, he was genuinely thinking of his nephew's well-being.

If it were another family's high school kid who declared they wanted to write web novels, Li Luo's advice would probably be similar to his eldest uncle's.

After all, only he himself knew his current situation; it was normal for his eldest uncle to misjudge.

Moreover, his uncle was a member of the writers' association, so it was understandable he'd be prejudiced against web novels. This was something difficult to correct through a simple conversation.

So Li Luo simply pretended to be mute.

Li Guohong and Lin Xiuhong also listened intently, nodding repeatedly, and then the topic was dropped.

After they had eaten and drunk their fill, Li Guoru's family rested for a short while before getting up to leave.

After Li Luo helped clean up the living room, he was pulled over to the sofa by Lin Xiuhong.

Li Guohong also sat down nearby. The family of three, rarely all together, held a family meeting.

"According to what your eldest uncle said, why don't you stop writing this book for now?"

Lin Xiuhong asked softly, "Didn't you tell me before that even if you signed a contract with the platform, you could stop writing whenever you wanted? They won't hold you to it, right?"

Next to her, Li Guohong chimed in, "Actually, I think you write quite well, but what your eldest uncle said also makes sense. At worst, you can write this book again after you get into college, just treat it as a pastime."

Listening to his parents, Li Luo sighed and then said, "Have you ever considered a possibility?"

"What?"

"That I'm earning money by writing this book."

"How much money could you possibly earn?" Lin Xiuhong looked at him suspiciously. "You're still in high school. Earning money isn't important; your studies come first."

Li Guohong also nodded in agreement.

After all, in their minds, how much could one earn from writing a book?

A kid just messing around, could he even make a hundred yuan a month?

Earning money was a small matter, but it would be a huge problem if it affected his studies.

"Ahem, it's like this." Li Luo took out his phone, logged into the Qidian app, and explained patiently to them, "Look, this chapter of mine is about two thousand words, and I've written over two hundred chapters now."

"And then, starting from around chapter one hundred, see this? The icon with a lock. From here on, if you want to read, you have to pay."

"A 2000-word chapter normally costs about ten cents. As long as enough people read it, you'll make money."

"But you can't be making that much from this." Li Guohong muttered, "What can you do with ten cents?"

Just as Li Guohong's voice fell, Li Luo suddenly pulled something out of his pants pocket and slapped it onto the coffee table.

Li Guohong and Lin Xiuhong were both stunned. Their gazes followed to the coffee table, and their expressions froze.

"What's this?" Lin Xiuhong reached out, picked up the stack of bills, and couldn't help but exclaim in shock, "Where did you get so much money?"

In Lin Xiuhong's memory, besides the 1,500 yuan she gave Li Luo for pocket money during the summer vacation, she hadn't given him any money since.

So these five thousand yuan definitely didn't come from them.

After all, Li Guohong had to rely on his private stash of cash just to smoke a few cigarettes. How could he have spare money to give to this kid Li Luo.

"Could it be... the manuscript fee?" Li Guohong took the wad of cash, his tone filled with doubt and disbelief. "For real? This has got to be several thousand, right?"

"This is five thousand yuan," Li Luo said.

"Five thousand yuan..." Lin Xiuhong was silent for a moment, but finally said, "Li Luo, I know this is very impressive. For someone your age to earn five thousand from writing a book, other kids don't even know what they're doing yet."

"But you've been writing this book since the end of June during summer vacation. How many months has it been?"

"Three or four months, right?"

In Lin Xiuhong's view, five thousand yuan was indeed a lot.

But earning five thousand in three or four months meant only twenty or thirty thousand a year.

Yes, it was a lot, an especially enormous sum for a high school student like Li Luo.

But if they could trade this income of twenty to thirty thousand a year, or a little under a hundred thousand over three years, in exchange for Li Luo getting into Qianjiang University.

Then to Lin Xiuhong, it was completely worth it.

But Li Luo's next words left Lin Xiuhong and Li Guohong completely dumbfounded.

"This five thousand yuan is just a part of last month's manuscript fee." Li Luo coughed twice and clarified, "The manuscript fee for August was over seven thousand, September's was twelve thousand, and the monthly fee from now on will only get higher and higher."

As his voice fell, the hand with which Li Guohong was holding the cash trembled slightly.

"What did you say?!" Lin Xiuhong, at the side, was even more astonished, her face full of disbelief, thinking she had misheard.

(End of this chapter)
